title: boardctl install: a git pre-commit hook that REJECTS a bad board (duplicate id / dangling ref), chained with the existing GitReins hook and bounded by a 30s timeout that SKIPS instead of blocking
reasoning:
WHAT AND WHY
A user who clones boardctl from GitHub, or runs it in a fleet repo, gets the
tool but NOT the protection: a board carrying a duplicate id or a dangling
depends_on reference can still be committed, and the damage only surfaces
later when a reader chokes on it. `boardctl validate` already detects every
one of these classes — nothing runs it at the moment a bad board would land.
This row is about TIMING, not detection.

EVIDENCE (2026-09-23, measured)
- `boardctl validate` on a healthy board: "RESULT: OK (0 warning(s))", exit 0.
  On the board damaged by the canopy incident it returned
  `[error] tasks.jsonl line 386: duplicate task id "DF-HERMES-CANOPY-52"
  (also line 382)` -> "RESULT: FAIL (1 error, 35 warnings)", exit 1.
  The detector exists, works, and names line numbers.
- BT-050 (open, P2) documents the writers that bypass `boardctl create`, and
  create ALREADY refuses a duplicate id (exit 2). So the guard is complete;
  it simply never runs at commit time.
- Fleet census 2026-09-23: **71 of 96** repos under /home/kara already carry
  `.git/hooks/pre-commit` — the GitReins Tier-1 hook, generated by
  `gitreins install`, whose binary path is PINNED at install time and which
  ends in a bare `exit $?`. Git allows exactly ONE pre-commit file, so a
  naive installer either clobbers that guard or gets clobbered by it.
  CHAINING IS THE CORE CONSTRAINT OF THIS ROW, not an option.

DELIVERABLE (tests-first per repo doctrine, with a RED ledger entry)
1. `boardctl hook run` — the hook's logic as a GO VERB, so it is testable
   rather than shell:
   - resolves the board like the sibling verbs (-C / repo root / board dir).
   - SKIPS CLEANLY (exit 0, one-line notice) when: not a board repo; the
     board file is absent; the boardctl binary cannot be resolved; or the
     staged set contains no board file (`--always` lints unconditionally).
     A hook that fails a commit because the tool is missing is worse than
     no hook at all.
   - STRICT lint on the staged board: duplicate id, dangling depends_on
     reference, unparseable line, out-of-vocabulary status -> FAIL (exit 1,
     naming the line numbers and the offending ids). The softer classes
     (priority vocabulary, legacy warnings) stay WARN and do NOT block.
   - BOUNDED: `--timeout` default **30s**; an expiry is exit 0 plus a loud
     SKIP notice. Rationale: the box may be saturated with running agents or
     the board may be large, and a lint hook must never wedge a commit.
   - Escape hatches, documented rather than hidden: `BOARDCTL_HOOK_SKIP=1`
     and `git commit --no-verify`.
2. `boardctl install [--hook] [--uninstall] [--force] [--global]`:
   - CHAINS: detect an existing pre-commit (the GitReins hook, or anything
     else), preserve it verbatim, and install a dispatcher that runs each
     hook in order and aggregates exit codes. The board-lint step runs FIRST
     so it reports before the slower guard. Never overwrite without --force.
   - `--global`: install once into a shared directory and point
     `core.hooksPath` at it, so a machine covers future clones; the per-repo
     install stays available.
   - Idempotent and reversible: a re-run is a no-op, `--uninstall` restores
     the previous hook byte-for-byte.
3. The "easy to add to repos" bundle: an example script under `examples/`,
   a README section showing `boardctl install` in three lines, and a SKILL
   that agents load stating the hook contract (what blocks, what warns, what
   skips) so a foreman that hits a rejection knows the REPAIR path instead of
   reflexively reaching for --no-verify.
4. A fleet-rollout mode for BT-053 to consume: install across many repos,
   report a per-repo outcome, never clobber.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- a duplicate id in the staged board -> `git commit` is REJECTED; the message
  names the id and both line numbers; `--no-verify` still works
- a dangling depends_on reference -> the same rejection path
- a clean board -> the commit proceeds unchanged
- no board / no binary / no board file staged -> exit 0, skip notice, commit
  proceeds
- lint exceeding the timeout (forced via a 1s `--timeout`) -> exit 0 + SKIP
  notice, commit proceeds
- in a repo carrying the GitReins hook, after install BOTH hooks run (prove
  the gitreins guard still blocks when its own config says it should), and
  `--uninstall` restores the original hook byte-identically
- re-running `boardctl install` is a no-op (no duplicated block, no diff)
- hermetic tests (no network, no real gitreins) pin every line above

SCOPE NOTE: the vocabulary of which validate classes are errors lives in
`validate` and must stay in ONE place — this row consumes it, never forks it.

title: validate silently yields nil for a non-array depends_on, so a dependency expressed in the wrong shape is invisible (BT-035 carries the string "[]")
reasoning:
FOUND 2026-09-23 while filing BT-052/053/054 (the board-lint pre-commit hook work),
so it belongs to that family rather than to a new investigation.

EVIDENCE
- Exactly ONE row on this board has a depends_on that is not an array: BT-035,
  which carries the STRING "[]" instead of an empty array. Every other row is
  either a real array or the key is absent.
- The tolerance is deliberate and documented in prose:
  internal/board/validate.go:220 — "depends_on). Non-array / malformed values
  yield nil." — and validate.go:171 feeds rowStringSlice(row, "depends_on") into
  the existence cross-check. A non-array therefore yields NO dependencies, the
  cross-check has nothing to test, and `boardctl validate` reports
  "RESULT: OK (0 warning(s))" for BT-035.
- The WRITE side is strict: internal/board/write.go:141 types DependsOn as
  []string, so boardctl's own writer could never emit this shape. This is
  legacy or hand-written data, exactly the population BT-050 describes.

WHY IT MATTERS (the class, not the single row)
The whole point of BT-054's hook is to stop a board carrying bad data from being
committed. A dependency expressed as a string is bad data that today round-trips
as "no dependencies" — silently. The failure is invisible in precisely the case
that hurts: if a row used the malformed shape with a REAL reference
("depends_on": "BT-019"), validate would emit no dangling-ref warning and a
reader would never see the edge at all. Tolerating the shape on READ is
defensible; tolerating it SILENTLY is not.

DELIVERABLE (small)
Add the class to `validate` (or to BT-054's strict lint) as a WARN:
"tasks.jsonl line N (task ID): depends_on is not an array — treated as no
dependencies". WARN and not error, so it cannot block a commit on legacy data by
itself; BT-054's hook owns the exit policy.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `boardctl validate` emits the new warning for BT-035 and still exits 0
- correcting BT-035 to [] makes the warning disappear
- a row with a real-but-malformed ref ("depends_on": "BT-019") is caught by the
  SAME warning — that is the case that actually protects a dependency edge
- no change to the existing dangling-ref check (BT-007 behaviour) and no new
  error introduced on any other row in this repo
